newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mostly down after new high.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mostly down after new high.

text.p: CME live cattle futures ended mostly lower as renewed profit taking and commercial hedge selling pulled futures down late after a new contract high was set in April. Feeders also posted a new high in April before following live cattle to mostly lower closes, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.150 cent per lb higher to 0.225 lower with only June up at 65.400 cents. April set a contract high of 70.800 cents before slipping to end steady at 70.300 cents.
April feeder cattle set a new contract high of 71.825 cents per lb early before futures ended 0.150 higher to 0.300 lower. Only April was up with May unchanged at 71.650 cents.

Live cattle ran up and set the new high in April following stronger cash markets before running into the profit taking and commercial hedge selling. Hedging started in April and spread to June, traders said.

"They (feedlots) figured they could sell the cattle in cash at $69 or they could sell them on the board for $70.50 - well it looks a little better on the board to sell them and deliver them," said Dale Benson, vice president and senior livestock analyst for Dean Witter.
Benson also cited rolling of long April positions into June which kept the latter supported somewhat late.
Back months also showed selling interest ahead of Friday's monthly USDA Cattle-on-Feed report, they said.

Early analysts' estimates on the report indicated on-feed numbers at major feedlots in the seven top cattle-feeding states ranging from 106 to 108 percent of last year. Placement estimates ranged from 100.5 to 107 percent of a year ago and marketings at 98 to 104.5 percent.
Early strength in futures reflected news that $69 per cwt was paid on fed cattle and boxed beef values at midday surged to five-week highs, traders said.
Heavy-weight choice beef values ran up to $105.13 at noon, a $2.29-jump from Monday's close and the highest levels since March 10. Prices on heavier-weight choice cuts have risen $6.72 since April 9.

In live cattle options, commercials headged early, buying August 63 puts and selling 67 calls. Commission house bought the June 64 straddle. Commercials sold June 71 and 72 puts late, pit sources said.

Feeder cattle futures followed the lead of deferred live cattle late with a rebound of sorts in corn futures prompting profit taking in the feeder cattle pit. Some sell stops added to the late setback, traders said.
Dean Witter, Refco and ING sold while LIT division of First Options was an active buyer during the day. ADM Investor Services bought August late, pit sources said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index fell $0.49 to $70.48 per cwt.
